content_text: [1/37 @DeRonin_] Andrej Karpathy: "90% of your AI coding bill is paying for context you didn't need to send" Here are 10 things senior AI engineers stopped wasting tokens on: 1. Auto-context loading 50 files for a 30-line fix: $1.20/turn for tokens you'll never read. 80% input waste, every session 2. Running Opus on lint, format, and rename tasks: $0.60 for what Haiku nails at $0.02. 30x overpay on the cleanup tier 3. Tool call loops that re-send the full repo on every retry: 5x context cost per agentic flow. fixing these alone cuts 30-50% of bills 4. Sonnet as the default model: Kimi 2.6 matches its quality on most coding tasks at 1/6 the cost. defaulting to Sonnet in 2026 is leaving 60-70% on the table 5. Streaming responses on stable-prefix workflows: kills your prompt cache. you pay 10x for tokens that should have cost cents 6. "Just in case" file includes: 80,000-token prompts that should be 3,000. context bloat is the silent budget killer 7. Per-session knowledge rebuilding: 10 min writing a SKILL.md once vs paying agents to re-figure out your environment every run. $4 vs $0.30 per execution 8. Single-model setups: premium tier on every task is the most expensive mistake in AI coding right now 9. Asking 10 small questions one at a time: 10 separate input prefix charges vs one batched call. 70-90% savings on routine workflows 10. Buying Claude Pro + ChatGPT Plus + Cursor Pro: you seriously use one. the other two are habit, not utility what actually compounds instead: - context discipline (grep before fetching, always) - prompt caching on every stable prefix - multi-model routing (Kimi 2.6 default, Opus for the 10%) - graduated skills via SKILL.md files - profiling tool calls before optimizing prompts - the routing mindset (right model for right task) in 12 months, the gap between developers shipping on $200/month and $4,000/month budgets won't be skill it'll be how well they route study this. --- [2/37 @0xCodez] @DeRonin_ another solid workshop by Andrej Karpathy, thanks for sharing brother ! --- [3/37 @Hiraweb3] @DeRonin_ clean execution beats flashy tools every time --- [4/37 @zhuren1992] @DeRonin_ Context discipline is the new alpha for AI coding budgets. --- [5/37 @MindTheGapMTG] @DeRonin_ Token routing saves 20%. Proper constraint files save 80%. The real cost isn't which model you call, it's your agent burning 50K tokens re-discovering your codebase every session because nobody wrote down the architecture decisions. The other 90% is your time. --- [12/37 @marmot_sh] @DeRonin_ We built marmot in part to offload lower-cognitive work from primary agents to lower cost models and to minimise context bloat https://t.co/7iZIO9Yihp --- [13/37 @leaf_sanren] 谁敢想，这是一年前的视频了都，但都不过时。我翻出来当时的notebook LM笔记，大家共勉： 第一，LLM 不是一个“答案机器”，更像一个随时可调用的思考搭子。 Karpathy 很少把它当成一次性问答工具，而是不断让它解释、改写、对比、补全、生成候选方案，再由自己判断。这里的关键不是“让 AI 替你思考”，而是让它扩大你的思考带宽。 第二，很多人只关心 prompt，但他其实更重视 context。 同一个问题，你给不给背景、文件、约束、目标，结果完全不是一个东西。尤其是长文、代码、论文、文档类任务，真正重要的不是一句神奇提示词，而是你有没有把材料、标准和边界讲清楚。 第三，他用 LLM 的方式很“分层”。 简单问题直接问；需要事实的任务结合搜索；需要处理材料的任务上传文件；需要执行的任务交给代码工具；需要长期复用的任务再沉淀成固定流程。 这点挺重要的，因为很多人一上来就想找“最强模型”，但其实应该先判断任务属于哪一层。 第四，代码场景里，他不是让 AI 一口气“帮我做完整项目”。 更像是：先让 AI 读代码、解释结构、定位相关文件、提出修改方案，然后小步实现，再看 diff、跑测试、继续修。 这其实不像 prompt 技巧，更像工程管理。AI 写代码越强，人越需要会拆任务、会验收、会控制风险。 第五，他对 LLM 的态度并不迷信。 视频里很多地方能感觉到，他会频繁 cross-check，会让模型给多个版本，会自己保留最终判断。 这可能是普通用户和高手最大的区别：普通人拿 AI 输出当答案，高手拿 AI 输出当候选材料。 很多人还在把 LLM 当聊天框用，问一句，等一句。 但 Karpathy 展示的是另一种用法：把 LLM 当成一个可以参与搜索、阅读、写作、编码、学习和创作的通用工作界面。 真正值得学的不是“他用了哪些产品”，而是这套习惯： 给足上下文， 拆小任务， 让模型生成多个候选， 自己做判断， 再把高频任务沉淀成流程。 这可能也是现在普通 AI 用户和高级 AI 用户最明显的分水岭。 不是谁背了更多 prompt，而是谁更会把自己的判断、材料和工作流组织起来。 --- [14/37 @abxxai] @DeRonin_ prompt caching getting killed by streaming is a sneaky one --- [15/37 @realtechodyssey] @DeRonin_ The cost problem is really a runtime design problem...uncontrolled context, repeated discovery, weak caching, and no model routing policy compound quickly. --- [16/37 @manojvasi7777] @DeRonin_ Built TokenTelemetry for @OpenAI, @AnthropicAI, @GoogleAI, @cursor_ai & Copilot workflows. One tactic that’s quietly compounding for me: dynamic context versioning. Instead of static SKILL.md or full greps, I maintain tiny “diff snapshots” (think: git-style summaries of the last N changes to key modules). Before a task, the agent first pulls only the delta relevant to the ticket (via a simple embedding index on commit messages + changed files). For a refactor in auth flow, it loads the 400-token summary of “what changed since last stable version” instead of 20k tokens of current code + history. Now wht if we treated agent sessions like git branches? Fork a lightweight context branch per feature, merge insights back to main memory layer on success, and let agents “rebase” cheaply on conflicts?!? No more per-session rediscovery, and you get audit trails for free. --- [29/37 @ChUd94747] @DeRonin_ Complete nonsense. I use Opus with full context and a €140/mo Ultra sub.
